reviewed_by: Claude general-purpose subagent, blind judgment reviewer (packet-only: competency text + rendered samples, no generator source), 2026-07-27 re-review batch

samples_reviewed.question_text: Compare the numbers: 3 ___ 1. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?
Compare the numbers: 3 ___ 1. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?
Compare the numbers: 1 ___ 1. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?
Compare the numbers: 1 ___ 3. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?
Compare the numbers: 1 ___ 2. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?

competency_fulfillment.rationale: Each sample directly performs the named act of comparing two numbers, e.g. seed 45 'Compare the numbers: 1 ___ 3. Which sign is correct: >, <, or =?' keyed '<'. The task asks for a relational symbol between exactly two quantities, which is precisely the verb and object of the competency, and every key I checked is relationally correct.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All three relational outcomes are represented, greater at seeds 42 and 43, equal at seed 44 with '1 ___ 1', and less at seeds 45 and 46, which is good. What is missing is any comparison involving the teen numbers the wording explicitly licenses; no sample places 11 through 20 on either side of the blank, so the pedagogically hard half of the stated domain is never exercised.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The stem is short and the symbol legend '>, <, or =' is helpfully restated, which suits Quarter 1 of Grade 1. However every item carries the distractor 'cannot be determined', an abstract logic-test phrase that a Grade 1 pupil in the first quarter cannot decode and that is never a valid answer, so it functions as noise rather than as a diagnostic distractor.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: Seeds 42 and 43 emit the byte-identical stem 'Compare the numbers: 3 ___ 1' and differ only in the shuffle of the option keys, so two of five draws are the same item. There is also a single presentation mode throughout: no 'which number is greater' wording, no comparison of two counted sets of objects, and no number-line or block-model framing.

competency_alignment.rationale: There is no observable difficulty gradient across seeds 42 to 46; every operand is drawn from the set {1, 2, 3}, so an item comparing 1 and 2 sits at the same trivial level as one comparing 3 and 1. A competency that reaches to 20 should progress from small single digits to crossing ten and then to teen-versus-teen, and none of that ladder is present.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The competency's stated ceiling is 20 but the largest number appearing anywhere in the five samples is 3. Operands are confined to 1, 2 and 3, so roughly eighty-five percent of the licensed numeric range is never generated and a student could master this bank without ever comparing a two-digit number.
